summary: The factory supervisor's Tick() reads intake/ off the local base branch with no fetch, so a GitHub-side merge (a promoted order, a dependency shipping) is invisible until a person pulls — in the pilot this held up a merged order for a day. This change adds one `git fetch <remote> <branch>` at the start of every pass (ADR-010, 2B stays the decision; fetch-before-read is an implementation detail under it, not a new structural decision), then reads intake/ at the remote-tracking ref `<remote>/<branch>` instead of the bare local branch. `--remote` defaults to `origin`; `--no-fetch` or a repository with no remote by that name reads the local branch exactly as today, with zero behavior change for every existing test fixture (none of which configure a remote). A fetch that fails for a remote that does exist (network, credentials) logs one line and the pass goes on from the last-fetched ref; it never parks or fails an order, and it never pulls, checks out, or resets the person's own working tree, index, or branch.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given a pass, when it starts, the supervisor MUST run `git fetch <remote> <branch>` exactly once and read intake/ at `<remote>/<branch>`. `--remote` defaults to `origin`.
examples: `loom factory run --once` with no `--remote` fetches `origin main` once before reading intake/.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given an order promoted to `ready` on the remote only, the next pass MUST claim it with no pull by a person, and the claim's `sourceCommit` MUST equal the fetched commit.
Given a claim, its worktree's branch MUST start from `<remote>/<branch>` at that commit when the order sets no `base-branch` of its own.
Given the person's checkout, a pass MUST NOT change its branch, index, or working tree, including uncommitted changes and local unpushed commits.

Given a fetch that fails (no network, no remote by that name, bad credentials), the pass MUST go on from the last fetched `<remote>/<branch>` and print exactly one line saying the fetch failed and why. It MUST NOT park or fail any order.

Given a repository with no remote by the configured name, or `--no-fetch`, the supervisor MUST read the local `<branch>` exactly as today, with no fetch attempted and no new output. Every existing test MUST keep passing with no change to what it asserts.
Given a running or waiting order, a fetch that moves `<remote>/<branch>` MUST NOT change it. The order MUST keep its claimed `sourceCommit`; only `loom factory rerun` takes a newer version.
Given `templates/claude-feature-team/intake/README.md`, it MUST say orders are read from the remote after a fetch, that a promotion must be pushed, and how `--no-fetch` restores the old behavior.

Given the change is complete, every new or changed function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail, `go test ./...` and the lint MUST pass, and no file outside `scope.paths` MUST change, excepting this run's own delivery record under `docs/features/factory-fetch-each-pass/`.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: A fetch adds at most one network call per pass. At the default 30 s interval that is two calls a minute.

The fetch uses the repository's already-configured remote and the person's own git credentials (via the ambient git credential helper); it sends nothing new and introduces no secret or token handling.

outOfScope: Pulling, merging, or rebasing the person's own checkout.
Fetching more often than once per pass.
`loom factory status` or `loom factory inbox` fetching — both keep reading the ledger and whatever `<remote>/<branch>` (or local branch) the last `run` pass left in place.

`loom factory rerun`'s own intake read (`readCommittedIntake` in cmd/loom/cmd/factory.go) fetching — it keeps reading the bare configured branch exactly as today; only the supervisor's own Tick() fetches.

boundedContext.owning: Factory supervisor — order lifecycle and ledger (ADR-010)
crossings: internal/worktree (git adapter: Repository implementation gains Fetch and Remotes)
cmd/loom/cmd (CLI flag surface: new --remote and --no-fetch flags on `loom factory run`)

affectedComponents.reason: Add Fetch(remote, branch string) error, following Push's existing pattern (context timeout, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, wrapped stderr); add Remotes() ([]string, error) via `git remote` (local-only, no network) so the supervisor can tell 'no remote by that name' apart from 'fetch failed reaching one that exists'.

Repository interface gains Remotes() ([]string, error) and Fetch(remote, branch string) error (consumer-defined, architecture-guardrails #1); Intake struct gains a Ref string field (the ref intake/ was actually read at) alongside the existing Commit field; ReadIntake sets Ref: branch.

Config gains Remote string and NoFetch bool; add DefaultRemote = "origin"; New() defaults an empty Remote to DefaultRemote; Tick() calls a new fetchIntakeRef() helper before ReadIntake instead of passing s.config.IntakeBranch directly.

claimWork, claim, and claimFor change from taking a bare commit string to taking the whole Intake (Commit + Ref travel together — Fowler's Introduce Parameter Object), so claimFor can default an order's base-branch to committed.Ref (the fetched remote-tracking ref) instead of the bare s.config.IntakeBranch, satisfying AC3.

factoryFlags gains remote string and noFetch bool; register --remote (default factory.DefaultRemote) and --no-fetch on factoryRunCmd; thread both into factory.Config in newFactorySupervisor; extend factoryRunCmd.Long to document the fetch-before-read behavior.

New tests for Fetch (updates origin/<branch>; a failure carries git's stderr) and Remotes (empty on a bare repo; lists a name once `git remote add` is run), following the existing bare-upstream-as-remote pattern already in this file.

New Tick-level tests for: fetch runs once per pass and reads the remote-tracking ref; a remote-only promoted order is claimed with no local pull; a claim with no explicit base-branch starts from <remote>/<branch>; a failing fetch continues and prints one line; no-remote and --no-fetch read the local branch with zero behavior change; a running/waiting order's sourceCommit survives a later fetch. Also update the existing call at line ~180 (`claimFor(candidate, committed.Commit)`) to the new `claimFor(candidate, committed)` signature.

newTestFactory/newSupervisor build a repo and Config with no remote configured — the exact fixture AC6 must hold against unchanged. May need a small helper for a bare-repo-as-upstream variant so the new fetch tests can push to an upstream the fixture's clone tracks.

AC8: the 'Enforced at pickup, by `loom factory` (ADR-010)' section (lines 91-97) must say orders are read from the remote after a fetch, that a promotion must be pushed, and how --no-fetch restores the old local-branch-only behavior.

No amendment needed — fetch-before-read is an implementation detail under Decision 2B ('read intake/ committed on base-branch, never the working tree'), not a new structural decision. Confirmed by reading the ADR; flagged here only so the developer doesn't open a new ADR unnecessarily.

dataModelChanges.description: Claim.BaseBranch's default value (set in claimFor when an order names no base-branch of its own) changes from the bare intake branch to the fetched remote-tracking ref (e.g. origin/main instead of main). The field's shape and persistence in the ledger are unchanged — only its default content differs, and only for orders that omit base-branch.

architecturalFlags: Repository interface gains Remotes and Fetch, both consumer-defined in internal/factory and implemented by internal/worktree.Git — matches architecture-guardrails #1 (UseCases define interfaces, Adapters implement them). internal/factory must not gain a production import of internal/worktree to support this (it has none today); keep that direction intact — any 'is there a remote' decision belongs in the Repository interface, not in a type or error sentinel shared across the boundary.

Fetch must reuse Push's existing network-call pattern in internal/worktree/manage.go: an explicit context.WithTimeout, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and an error wrapped with git's own stderr (architecture-guardrails #5 — every network call needs an explicit timeout).

Remotes must stay a local-only, un-timed call (`git remote`, no network) — it exists purely to distinguish 'no remote configured by this name' (AC6, silent fallback) from 'a remote exists but the fetch to it failed' (AC5, one logged line); conflating the two into Fetch's own error would either spam logs for everyday local-only repos or silently hide a real credential/network failure.

developer: internal/worktree/manage.go: add `const fetchTimeout = 5 * time.Minute` next to pushTimeout, and `func (g *Git) Fetch(remote, branch string) error` using context.WithTimeout(fetchTimeout), GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, and an error wrapped with the command's combined stderr output, mirroring Push exactly.

internal/factory/supervisor.go: add `func (s *Supervisor) fetchIntakeRef() (string, error)`: return `s.config.IntakeBranch` unchanged when `s.config.NoFetch`; otherwise call `s.deps.Repository.Remotes()`, return the bare branch unchanged when `s.config.Remote` is not among them (AC6); otherwise call `s.deps.Repository.Fetch(s.config.Remote, s.config.IntakeBranch)`, logging one `s.say(...)` line naming the remote, branch, and error on failure (AC5) without returning an error; then return `s.config.Remote + "/" + s.config.IntakeBranch` if that ref resolves via `s.deps.Repository.ResolveCommit`, else fall back to the bare branch (covers a first-ever fetch failing before any remote-tracking ref exists).

edgeCases.case: The person's checkout has uncommitted changes or local commits not yet pushed.
edgeCases.handling: Fetch only updates the remote-tracking ref; it never touches HEAD, the index, or the working tree, so both stay exactly as they were (AC4).

edgeCases.case: The repository has no remote named --remote (default origin) at all — e.g. every existing test fixture.
edgeCases.handling: fetchIntakeRef checks Remotes() membership before attempting Fetch; absent, it returns the bare local branch with no fetch call and no new output, byte-for-byte today's behavior (AC6).
fetchIntakeRef short-circuits to the bare local branch before even checking Remotes().

edgeCases.case: The named remote exists but the fetch fails (no network, bad credentials, remote renamed server-side).
edgeCases.handling: Fetch's error is logged as one line via s.say(...); the pass continues and reads whatever <remote>/<branch> last resolved to (or the bare branch if that ref has never existed), never parking or failing an order (AC5).

edgeCases.case: The remote exists but has never been fetched before (first-ever pass, and that first fetch fails).
edgeCases.handling: ResolveCommit("<remote>/<branch>") also fails since the ref never existed; fetchIntakeRef falls back to the bare local branch rather than erroring the whole Tick.

edgeCases.case: An order is running or waiting when a later fetch moves the remote branch forward.
edgeCases.handling: The order's Claim (including SourceCommit and BaseBranch) was fixed at claim time and is never recomputed by continuation()/relaunch(); only RequestRerun re-reads intake and reclaims (AC7).

edgeCases.case: An order sets its own base-branch explicitly (every current fixture does: base-branch: main).
edgeCases.handling: claimFor only falls back to committed.Ref when order.BaseBranch is empty; an explicit base-branch is untouched by this change.

edgeCases.case: `loom factory status`, `loom factory inbox`, and `loom factory rerun` are invoked between supervisor passes.
edgeCases.handling: Per the spec's resolved Open Question, none of these fetch; they keep reading the ledger and whichever ref (remote-tracking or local) the last `loom factory run` pass left resolved, via the unchanged readCommittedIntake/factoryArgs.branch path.

definitionOfDone: Every new or changed function (Supervisor.fetchIntakeRef, Supervisor.hasRemote, Git.Fetch, Git.Remotes, start.go's claimFor/claim/claimWork) has cyclomatic complexity below 7.
Every changed line is covered by a test that fails against the pre-change code and passes after (ADR-008).
The project's lint step passes with no new findings.
No file outside `scope.paths` (internal/factory/**, internal/worktree/**, cmd/loom/cmd/factory*.go, templates/claude-feature-team/intake/README.md, docs/features/factory-fetch-each-pass/**) changes.
`templates/claude-feature-team/intake/README.md` describes the fetch-before-read behavior, that a promotion must be pushed, and what `--no-fetch` restores.
A reviewer can push a promoted order to the remote only, run `loom factory run --once` with no local pull, and see it claimed with the fetched commit as its sourceCommit.
openQuestions: Spec's own open question: should `loom factory status` and `loom factory inbox` also fetch? Assumption carried into this analysis (unresolved — confirm before merge): no. Both keep reading the ledger and whatever `<remote>/<branch>` (or local branch) the last supervisor pass left resolved; `loom factory rerun`'s own intake read also stays unchanged for the same reason.
